hypotheses.reasoning: Login failures begin when auth-svc lost capacity: auth-svc-3 failed its liveness probe and restarted at 12:06:48 (capacity 3/4, #1337). The first account-svc retry for POST /tokens follows at 12:06:52 (#1346). account-svc then retries auth-svc with no backoff (delay 0ms, 'retrying immediately, backoff disabled', #1438, #1503), multiplying load on the remaining instances. auth-svc goes to 3.2x-5x baseline inflight (~713-752) and sheds load with 'queue full' 503s (#1397, #1441, #1544, #1639). Edge-proxy then returns 503 on POST /login after account-svc retries are exhausted (#1376, #1518, #2226). The sustained non-recovery matches the retry amplification keeping auth-svc saturated after the instance came back at 12:07:32 (#1385). The trigger itself (why auth-svc-3 failed liveness) is not visible in the logs. The /search 500s and catalog S3 503s are a separate path (search-api/catalog-svc) and do not cause the login failures.

account-svc heap was at 83% of 2048MiB with a concurrent mark cycle starting at 12:03:39 (#979), and auth-svc-3 then failed liveness at 12:06:48 (#1337). Memory or GC pressure on auth-svc-3 could explain the restart, but there is no OOM or heap error on auth-svc and account-svc has 0 error+ lines, so this is only a weak alternative for the trigger.

verdict.recommendedAction: Stabilize auth-svc first: remove the immediate retries in account-svc's AuthClient (#1438, #1503) and add exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget, so retries stop multiplying traffic into auth-svc. Confirm auth-svc inflight returns to baseline and POST /login 503s stop at edge-proxy. Then find out why auth-svc-3 failed its liveness probe at 12:06:48 (check its heap, GC and probe timeouts), and check account-svc's heap trend (#979). The /search 500s from catalog-svc S3 503 throttling (#1009, #1052) are a separate issue to triage on their own.
